input.question: When did straight white teeth become a status symbol?
input.ground_truth: I'm guessing this is a thing in the States? As with so many things, it probably started to become a status symbol as soon as famous people started doing it. This being said, the super white teeth American TV stars and politicians tend to have is not really a thing here in Europe (is this changing?). So it's not a status symbol everywhere. Even teeth you take very good care of should have a slightly yellow tint to them. It's the natural color of the teeth. By making them completely white you're making them look like something that isn't the color of teeth.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Question: When did straight white teeth become a status symbol?

Answer:

Okay, let’s imagine you have a toy car. At first, all the toy cars look the same, but then some people start making their toy cars shiny and straight. Suddenly, everyone thinks those shiny and straight toy cars are extra special and cool.

It’s kind of like that with people’s teeth. Long ago, people didn’t care so much about whether their teeth were straight or not. But as time went on, some people started having their teeth fixed to look straight and white, like shiny toy cars. When other people saw this, they thought, “Wow, that looks nice!” So, having straight and white teeth started to become something that made people look important or fancy, like a cool badge. That’s when straight white teeth became a status symbol.
